evals.name: messy-java-full-review
evals.prompt: Can you review our test automation framework? It's the Java/TestNG/Selenium repo at .claude/skills/automation-framework-review-skill-creator/evals/fixtures/messy-framework (relative to the repo root c:\Users\knysh\source\repos\evals-demo). Give me the full issues list plus the checklist-tab table at the end. Save the review to review.md and the checklist table to checklist.md in the skill-creator workspace eval directory you're given.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown issues-list document citing concrete file:line evidence for the seeded defects in messy-framework.manifest.md (God Base Class, missing business-step layer, layer-boundary leakage, raw-type leakage, cross-file sibling duplication, swallowed exceptions, hardcoded sleeps, fragile/raw locators, naming outliers, scratch/WIP test files, etc.), each tagged [Impact: .. | Effort: ..], with a FIRST-principles table and a Recommended Actions rollup, plus a separate checklist-tab table (Section | Check | Status | Comments) covering only code-verifiable rows. No clean dimensions praised; no placeholder 'no violations found' headings.
assertions: Flags BasePage.java as a God Base Class / SRP violation bundling multiple unrelated responsibilities (navigation, waits, assertions, popups, data I/O, misc utilities)

Identifies a missing business-step/flow layer, citing that tests inline the same create-order / register-user sequences directly via page-object calls (at least 3 of the 5 known occurrences across CreateOrderTests.java, RegisterUserTests.java, InvoiceLookupTests.java)

Identifies layer-boundary leakage: at least 2 of the 4 test files that import org.openqa.selenium.WebDriver/WebElement and call driver.findElement directly instead of going through a page object (ProductGridTests.java, InvoiceLookupTests.java, FullProductLifecycleTests.java, FullInvoiceBillingCycleTests.java)
Identifies raw WebElement/List<WebElement> leakage from public page-object methods (e.g. BasePage.getRawElement/getRawElements, UserManagement.getFirstResultRow, OrderHandler.getAllOrderRows)

Identifies cross-file sibling duplication across the 4 *ModifyPage classes (UserModifyPage, OrderModifyPage, ProductModifyPage, InvoiceModifyPage) with near-identical method bodies, not just a single-file God Base Class finding
Reports a quantified hardcoded-sleep count backed by a grep (expects a count in the 30s-40s range across ~10 files, not just 'some sleeps exist')

Reports a quantified empty-catch-block / swallowed-exception count backed by a grep (expects a count in the 30s-40s range across ~9 files), and separately flags BasePage.compareElementText's empty catch as a verification utility masking failure as a false match
Reports a quantified count of assertion-free test methods (expects 4, e.g. in ProductGridTests.java and InvoiceLookupTests.java)
Flags the 3 giant multi-feature single-@Test-method test classes (FullAdminWorkflowTests, FullProductLifecycleTests, FullInvoiceBillingCycleTests), each 150+ lines covering many unrelated features
Flags the nonzero CI retry count (testng.xml retryCount=3 + RetryListener) as masking flakiness, with no quarantine/tracking mechanism
Flags the scratch/WIP test package (com.acme.crm.wip) as not excluded from the TestNG suite scan
Flags hardcoded plaintext credentials/environment values (config.properties, DbConnector.java) with no environment-switching mechanism
Gives a locator-strategy distribution with real counts/percentages (not just an impression), roughly matching the ~31%/31%/38% positional/id/css split
Does NOT include a heading or paragraph praising any clean dimension (e.g. no 'the core layers are well separated' or similar fluff) — every surviving heading names a problem
Every individual finding is tagged with [Impact: High/Medium/Low | Effort: High/Medium/Low] immediately after its heading, using only those three legal values
Produces a FIRST-principles table (Fast/Independent/Repeatable/Self-validating/Timely) with a verdict and evidence for each letter

Produces a separate checklist-tab table with exact columns Section | Check | Status (+/-) | Comments, containing only rows this review's evidence actually backs (not the Tools/Strategy/AI-Usage sections)
Checklist table includes a '-' row for 'Unconditional waits are not a common practice' and for 'Framework complies with SOLID' given the God Base Class finding

evals.name: medium-python-mixed-signal-review
evals.prompt: We have a Python/pytest/Playwright hybrid API+UI framework for our SubTrack Admin product at .claude/skills/automation-framework-review-skill-creator/evals/fixtures/medium-framework (relative to repo root c:\Users\knysh\source\repos\evals-demo). Please audit it against best practices and tell us what's actually wrong — we already think some parts of it (fixtures, test-data builders, locators) are solid so don't waste our time relitigating what's fine. Save your findings as review.md in the eval directory.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown issues-list document that catches the 10 seeded defects in medium-framework.manifest.md (missing business-step layer, raw-requests layer leakage in 2 of 4 API test files, raw-token domain-representation inconsistency in the same 2 files as a DISTINCT finding, cross-file sibling page-object duplication, shared mutable module-level state / order dependency, 2 assertion-free tests, 2 bare except:pass blocks, nonzero reruns with no flaky-tracking, 2 naming outliers among page objects, 1 hardcoded plaintext-looking API key) while NOT flagging any of the 7 deliberately clean practices (fixture-based DI with no God Base Class, builder-pattern test-data factories used consistently, zero hardcoded sleeps, consistent semantic locators, current Playwright pin, trace-on-retry + published HTML report, clean *Page naming on 8 of 10 files).
assertions: Flags a missing business-step/flow layer across at least 3 of the 4 known test functions (test_update_account_name, test_update_account_status, test_update_ticket_priority, test_update_subscription_seats) that each inline the same create->open->modify->save->assert sequence

Flags layer-boundary leakage in test_billing_sync_api.py and test_ticket_export_api.py (raw `requests` import/calls bypassing the existing *Client wrapper classes), and explicitly notes the sibling API test files that use the wrappers correctly (contrast, not a blanket API-layer complaint)

Flags the raw-token / domain-representation inconsistency in the SAME two files (test_billing_sync_api.py, test_ticket_export_api.py) as a DISTINCT finding from the raw-requests layering issue, not merged into one bullet
Flags cross-file sibling duplication across the 4 *_modify_page.py classes (account, contact, ticket, subscription) with near-identical bodies differing only in label text

Flags the shared module-level mutable state in test_ticket_lifecycle.py (_CREATED_TICKET_IDS list) as a test-independence / order-dependency violation, ideally noting the IndexError that results from running the dependent test in isolation
Reports a count of assertion-free tests matching or close to 2 (test_delete_account_removes_from_list, test_delete_account)

Flags the 2 bare except:pass blocks (in test_ticket_export_api.py's comparison helper and test_admin_console_nav.py's comparison helper) as swallowed exceptions in verification/comparison utilities specifically
Flags the nonzero pytest-rerunfailures retry config (reruns=2) in pytest.ini and CI as masking flakiness with no quarantine/tracking mechanism
Flags exactly the 2 naming outliers (AdminConsole, SettingsScreen) among page objects without over-generalizing to claim the whole pages/ package is inconsistent (8 of 10 follow *Page correctly)

Flags the hardcoded plaintext-looking API key in config.py (INVOICING_PROVIDER_API_KEY = "sk-fake1234567890") as inconsistent with the os.getenv() pattern used by every other credential in the same class
Does NOT flag the fixture-based DI/composition in conftest.py as a God Base Class or inheritance-chain problem (it is deliberately clean)
Does NOT flag the builder-pattern test-data factories (AccountBuilder, ContactBuilder, TicketBuilder, SubscriptionBuilder) as missing or inconsistent
Does NOT claim hardcoded sleeps exist anywhere in the fixture (there are deliberately zero)
Does NOT flag the locator strategy as inconsistent or fragile (all page objects use get_by_role/get_by_label/get_by_test_id/get_by_text consistently)
Does NOT include fluff/praise sentences for the clean dimensions (fixtures, factories, locators, diagnostics) in the verdict paragraph — the user explicitly asked not to relitigate what's fine
Every finding is tagged with [Impact: High/Medium/Low | Effort: High/Medium/Low] using only those three legal values

evals.name: clean-typescript-false-positive-check
evals.prompt: Review the Playwright/TypeScript test framework in .claude/skills/automation-framework-review-skill-creator/evals/fixtures/clean-framework (relative to repo root c:\Users\knysh\source\repos\evals-demo) against our usual best-practices checklist (layering, SOLID, DRY, test design, locators, error handling, waits, naming). We think this one's in pretty good shape but want a second opinion before sign-off. Save the review as review.md.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown issues-list document that reports little to nothing wrong (this fixture is deliberately clean) and, critically, does NOT fabricate findings in dimensions that are genuinely clean (no God Base Class claim, no missing-flow-layer claim, no layer-leakage claim, no sibling-duplication claim, no hardcoded-sleep claim, no fragile-locator claim, no naming-inconsistency claim about EntityModifyPanel or submitLoginAttempt — both explicitly correct by design per the manifest's false-positive list). It is acceptable and correct for the review to surface the few genuine unseeded bugs noted in the manifest (missing package-lock.json breaking `npm ci`, tsconfig lib omitting ES2022 breaking the `cause` property typecheck, duplicated nextSuffix() helper across two factory files, shallow assertions in a few tests, UI-seeding where an API path already exists) — those are real findings a thorough review should catch, not false positives. The FIRST-principles table should show mostly passing verdicts.
assertions: Does NOT claim a God Base Class exists (BasePage.ts is deliberately slim: goto()/waitForLoad() only)
Does NOT claim a missing business-step/flow layer exists (src/flows/orderFlows.ts, userFlows.ts, authFlows.ts are the real flow layer and every test uses them)
Does NOT claim layer-boundary leakage into tests (no test file imports @playwright/test directly per the fixture's design)

Does NOT claim cross-file sibling duplication between OrderModifyPage and UserModifyPage as an uncontrolled DRY violation (they share logic via the composed EntityModifyPanel helper, which is the correct fix pattern, not the defect)
Does NOT claim hardcoded sleeps exist (zero page.waitForTimeout() calls in the fixture)
Does NOT claim fragile/positional locators exist (fixture uses only getByRole/getByLabel/getByTestId)
Does NOT flag EntityModifyPanel for not ending in 'Page' as a naming inconsistency (it is explicitly documented as intentionally not a page object)
Does NOT flag submitLoginAttempt as a duplicate/inconsistent second login method (it is a distinct, correctly-named method for the negative-login test path)
Does NOT flag the per-test UI login in adminSession/standardSession fixtures as a missing storageState optimization framed as a defect (an optional enhancement note is fine; calling it wrong is not)
Does NOT claim test-data cleanup/teardown is missing (the createdRecords fixture registers and tears down all 4 data-creating specs)
Does NOT claim retries/trace capture are misconfigured (retries: 0 deliberately pairs with trace: 'on-first-retry'... this is documented and correct)
If thorough, correctly surfaces the missing package-lock.json / npm ci mismatch (CI runs `npm ci` but no lockfile is committed) as a genuine, non-seeded defect
If thorough, correctly surfaces the tsconfig.json lib omitting ES2022 breaking the `cause` property typecheck in errors.ts as a genuine, non-seeded defect
If thorough, correctly surfaces the duplicated nextSuffix() helper across orderFactory.ts and userFactory.ts as a real cross-file duplication worth extracting
Produces a FIRST-principles table with mostly passing/clean verdicts, not manufactured failures

The verdict-up-front paragraph does not read as a tour of what's good (no 'the architecture is clean, locators are stable, waits are solid' style praise) — if genuinely little is wrong, it says so briefly rather than touring strengths

Total finding count is low (roughly 0-5 real findings), consistent with this being a deliberately clean fixture — a review padding this out with 10+ findings to seem thorough is a failure mode to flag
